$comment: Single source of truth for the fork's identity. Product name SKYCOT chosen 21 October 2026 (Foreman was the build-time placeholder). Changing a value = edit this file + `apps/desktop/package.json` productName (the one JSON seam), then run `node nondev/scripts/apply-brand.ts` to confirm. Runtime values are injected as T3CODE_* environment defaults by `nondev/brand/env.cjs`; upstream code keeps its own defaults, so every seam stays upstreamable.

updates.$comment: Where the Mac app looks for new SKYCOT versions. The ONLY source: env.cjs hands it on as T3CODE_SKYCOT_UPDATE_FEED; the desktop build bakes it into the app, the app refuses any other feed, and T3 Code's releases are refused everywhere (packages/skycot-brand/src/updateFeed.ts). null = no updates (today: there is no public, signed Mac download yet; the private repo above cannot serve one). To switch on, see docs/nondev/UPDATES.md: e.g. "https://skycot.com/downloads/mac/" (a folder serving latest-mac.yml + the signed zip/dmg) or "github:<owner>/<public-repo>". updateRepository above is the source repo (the CLI `update` command and Advanced mode's release links), not the app's feed.

modelManifest.$comment: Where the engine may refresh its list of AI models between releases. Upstream T3 Code fetches it hourly from its own GitHub repository, which would let T3 Tools decide which models SKYCOT offers, so SKYCOT never does: env.cjs hands this on as T3CODE_SKYCOT_MODEL_MANIFEST_URL and the engine (apps/server/src/skycot/modelManifestSource.ts) refuses anything that is not https or names T3 Code. null = use the manifest bundled with each build (refreshed by every upstream sync). To host our own later: an https URL serving the same JSON, e.g. "https://skycot.com/models/model-manifest.json".

telemetry.$comment: Leave both null until we own a PostHog project. While they are null, enabling telemetry at runtime sends nothing (an empty key is rejected locally) rather than reporting into upstream's project.
